item.title: Introducing WorldVQA
item.guid: title:introducing worldvqa
item.description: A benchmark for evaluating atomic visual world knowledge in Multimodal LLMs. Authors Kimi Team We are releasing WorldVQA , a new benchmark designed to measure the factual correctness of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While recent models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in visual reasoning and description, measuring their reliability regarding visual world knowledge remains a challenge.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: The agentic blind spot: detecting AI secret exfiltration
item.guid: title:the agentic blind spot detecting ai secret exfiltration
item.description: Originally published on ReclaimLLM: https://reclaimllm. com/blogs/detecting-ai-agent-secret-exfiltration-ad004 Why monitoring file-read tools misses agent execution loops: how coding agents use shell pipelines and shadow scripts like load_dotenv() — and how AD-004 detects them. The agentic blind spot: detecting AI secret exfiltration Most enterprise security tooling evaluates developer environments using static assumptions: inspect the repo with SAST, scan commits with git hooks, and monitor endpoint file system access. Autonomous AI coding agents render those assumptions obsolete. An agent is not a static script. It is an iterative reasoning engine paired with tool execution.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

Built as a native multimodal model, K2. 5 delivers state-of-the-art coding and vision capabilities and a self-directed agent swarm paradigm.

item.title: The Interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety. They seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build.
item.guid: title:the interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for ai safety they seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build
item.description: It’s hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them. Our goal is to be able to explain large language models’ behavior, and to use that understanding to identify problems that are hard to see from the outside, such as situations where a model’s stated reasoning differs from what it’s actually doing. Our early work focused on mapping the internal mechanisms of AI models. Today, we increasingly apply our methods to real models to understand how they think and why they behave the way they do. We’ve developed techniques that allow us to understand models’ inner workings in plain language, making it easier to detect unsafe behavior or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it. item.title: Echoes, With Evidence: a browser-sized ofrenda for stories worth keeping
item.guid: title:echoes with evidence a browser sized ofrenda for stories worth keeping
item.description: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built A remembered person can be a whole room: a radio playing during a blackout, orange peel on a kitchen table, a hand letting go of a bicycle saddle. Finding those moments should not require remembering the exact words used to describe them. Echoes, With Evidence is a small, local-first remembrance archive. You keep short stories on a table of illustrated cards, then search by a feeling, image, or idea. An open model finds related stories. Each result leads back to the words that were saved, with a title, person, date, and full source card.

item.title: Decode Is 300x Memory-Bound. Batching Fixes That Until the Context Gets Long.
item.guid: title:decode is 300x memory bound batching fixes that until the context gets long
item.description: I spent last week arguing about KV cache sizes. The useful follow-up is simpler: multiply the cache by the context length and you get the number that actually sets your throughput. Decode does not run out of FLOPs. It runs out of memory bandwidth, by a factor of about 300, and every GPU generation keeps it that way. Here is the arithmetic, computed rather than asserted, plus a script that reads your own model config and prints your ceiling. Decode is one FLOP per byte read For a dense model at batch size 1, generating one token means reading every weight tensor once and doing two multiply-adds per parameter.

item.title: Zero-Backend Client-Side RAG in the Browser with WebGPU, Transformers.js, MediaPipe, and OPFS
item.guid: title:zero backend client side rag in the browser with webgpu transformers js mediapipe and opfs
item.description: Original: https://codingcat. dev/post/client-side-webgpu-rag-transformers-js-mediapipe-opfs Most teams building semantic search or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for documentation portals reach straight for a cloud vector database and an external embedding API. That works fine until you need instant sub-10ms keystroke search, offline availability, or strict zero-egress privacy for user documents. With WebGPU compute shaders , Transformers. js v3 , Google MediaPipe , and the Origin Private File System (OPFS) , you can run the entire embedding, vector indexing, and synthesis pipeline directly inside the user's browser tab. The Mental Model: Local WebGPU Shaders + OPFS Binary Vector Cache Why did client-side embeddings feel sluggish three years ago?

item.title: The enterprise AI control plane: moving from risk to audit-ready
item.guid: title:the enterprise ai control plane moving from risk to audit ready
item.description: Originally published on ReclaimLLM: https://reclaimllm. com/blogs/enterprise-ai-coding-security-control-plane Why blanket AI bans fail: a four-layer defense across pre-execution hook DLP, governed gateways, customer-key encryption, and multi-cadence alerting. The enterprise AI control plane: moving from risk to audit-ready When security and compliance teams realize that autonomous AI coding agents can read . env files, execute shell extraction pipelines, and pipe credentials to external model providers, the initial enterprise reaction is often administrative restriction: ban AI coding tools or block provider domains at the firewall. This strategy fails in practice. Engineers under pressure to deliver software will route around network firewalls using personal hotspots, copy sensitive context into browser-based assistants, or disable internal security scanners.

item.title: Kimi Introduces Agent Swarm: Let 100 AI Agents Work for You
item.guid: title:kimi introduces agent swarm let 100 ai agents work for you
item.description: In 2025, if you walked into any AI conference, you may hear the same gospel: faster inference, longer context windows, cheaper inference costs. It's as if we've spent years perfecting the hammer, making it lighter, stronger, more precisely balanced, while never questioning the fact that the carpenter still has only two hands and twenty-four hours in a day. Now, Kimi introduces Agent Swarm. It is not a better hammer. It is a reconstruction of the entire workshop.

item.title: Passing the OTCA With 83: Half the Exam Is the SDK Pipeline
item.guid: title:passing the otca with 83 half the exam is the sdk pipeline
item.description: I wrote the longer version, with everything I read and what wasted my time, on my blog . You can run Prometheus perfectly in production and still fail the OTCA. If you've turned on auto-instrumentation or shipped telemetry to a Collector sidecar, you were inside the OpenTelemetry pipeline without ever being tested on how it works. The OpenTelemetry Certified Associate tests what happens inside it. I passed with 83 on the first attempt, one of the 15 CNCF certifications I did on the way to Golden Kubestronaut. Format and weights 60 multiple-choice questions, 90 minutes, pass at 75%.

item.title: Microsoft’s MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming and the 100 ms WASAPI Capture Budget
item.guid: title:microsoft s mai transcribe 2 streaming and the 100 ms wasapi capture budget
item.description: On 1 October 2026 Microsoft shipped MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, its first real-time speech-to-text model. It returns the first partial hypotheses in just over 100 ms of receiving audio, finalizes with roughly 0. 13 s of post-speech latency, and posts a 2. 5 % word-error rate on the Artificial Analysis streaming leaderboard—ahead of the previous Grok Voice Transcribe 2. 0 streaming entry. The model covers 60 languages with continuous automatic language detection and is priced at an introductory $0.
